why: All three checks confirm the finding; nothing refutes it. (1) VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md line 112 opens with the quoted sentence character-for-character: "For a `\"fresh\"` base, Claude Code keeps `origin/HEAD` current: when the repository hasn't been fetched in the last 24 hours, it fetches the default branch, capped at five seconds, and uses the locally cached ref if the fetch fails." I read the WHOLE line: its two remaining sentences REINFORCE rather than reverse the claim - "If no remote is configured, or `origin/HEAD` isn't cached locally and can't be fetched, the worktree falls back to your current local `HEAD`" (the half we DO implement) and "Before v2.1.208, a fresh worktree used whatever `origin/HEAD` was already cached locally" (which names our current behaviour exactly). The page is row 194 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude Code contract page, not Codex/MCP. (2) CITED CODE: worktree-git-plan.ts:39-53 is verbatim as claimed - for baseRef 'fresh' it returns exactly [{operation:'base-fresh', args:['-C',repoRoot,'rev-parse','origin/HEAD'], allowFailure:true}, {operation:'base', args:['-C',repoRoot,'rev-parse','HEAD']}]. No fetch, no last-fetch timestamp, no default-branch resolution. SessionManager.ts:10150 is the sole production call site (the only other hits are the import at :136 and worktree-git-plan.test.ts, which pins the exact argv - so the missing fetch is frozen by a test). (3) LAYER UP AND DOWN. Down: runWorktreeGit (SessionManager.ts:10020-10048) is the only git runner on this path; it spawns `git` with host-built argv under a read-only sandbox profile - it does not prepend or inject anything. Up: the WorktreeLeaseService policy.select at :10144-10161 just loops the candidates and takes the first non-empty sha; git.create (:10164) consumes that sha with `worktree add -b`. No fetch upstream. Repo-wide absence check with -a and a positive control: `grep -ranE "'fetch'|\"fetch\"" --include='*.ts' packages apps` returns only WebFetch permission-DSL tests and a schema fixture - zero git-fetch call sites; the same grep style DOES find `command: 'git'` at SessionManager.ts:10033 and eight git invocations in workspace/git-branches.ts (which also never fetches), so grep is reading these files. packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts contains neither 'fetch' nor 'origin/'. Sibling-subsystem check: there is no second worktree-creation path - session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts (EnterWorktree) routes through the same lease service, and no other module runs `git worktree add`. NOT an owner decision: inert-worklist section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions - none touches worktrees. NOT a deliberate product difference either: worktree-settings.ts:68-76 records the ONE intentional worktree deviation (bgIsolation default 'none' instead of 'worktree') and explicitly says of the other key "Documented default for `baseRef` is `\"fresh\"` and we match it" - so freshness is claimed, not disclaimed. definitions.ts:51-54 goes further and asserts the isolation contract is "already satisfied here: `worktreeBaseShaCandidates` resolves `origin/HEAD` first", a claim that is now stale against the page. The origin of the gap is visible: our contract distillation (2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:126) captured baseRef as '"fresh" default = origin/<default-branch>' with no fetch clause, and the implementing plan 2026-07-27-session-worktrees.md contains the word 'fetch' only in an instruction to fetch raw markdown - i.e. we built against the pre-v2.1.208 page and the upstream refresh behaviour landed afterwards. CONSEQUENCE verified separately from the identifier: `git rev-parse origin/HEAD` resolves refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, a purely local remote-tracking ref that only moves on fetch, so on a repo last fetched weeks ago every 'fresh' worktree branches off the stale cached commit with no error and no signal - exactly what the page says changed in v2.1.208.
correctedState: Confirmed with two precision fixes to the claim's wording. (a) 'no timeout anywhere on the worktree path' is too strong: every worktree git command DOES carry a 60s process timeout (SessionManager.ts:10043, `timeoutMs: 60_000`). What is absent is the doc's five-second cap specific to the freshness fetch - moot, because no fetch is issued at all. (b) 'sole call site' is right for production only; worktree-git-plan.test.ts:14-28 also calls it and pins the exact two-candidate argv, so the missing fetch is asserted by a test and any fix must update that test. Everything else stands: for baseRef 'fresh' the candidates are exactly `git -C <root> rev-parse origin/HEAD` (allowFailure) then `git -C <root> rev-parse HEAD`; there is no `git fetch`, no last-fetch staleness check and no default-branch resolution anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (verified with grep -a plus a positive control), and neither runWorktreeGit below nor WorktreeLeaseService/EnterWorktree above supplies one. Nessy therefore implements the pre-v2.1.208 behaviour the page calls out as changed, and it is not a recorded owner decision or a rebranding/product difference - worktree-settings.ts explicitly claims parity on baseRef while disclaiming only bgIsolation, and definitions.ts:51-54 carries a now-stale comment asserting the base-branch contract is satisfied.
